compiled_state.title: Hard-constraint immutability diff-check: coordination-pass rejected if hard_constraint items mutate
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Testing Mode
RED

## Story DD Coverage
This task is responsible for satisfying the following story done definitions:
- dd-4 (c5ef): items whose rationale.rule_ids cite a canon rule with hard_constraint=true have identical values pre- and post-coordination-pass; a diff check confirms zero mutations on those items
- dd-5 (c5ef): the updated artifact remains schema-conforming and re-runs the deterministic post-processor to refresh the checks block
- dd-6 (c5ef): unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Description
After the coordination-pass dispatch completes (T2), implement a diff-check step that:
1. Loads both first-pass and second-pass artifacts
2. For each item, checks if any rationale.rule_ids citation references a canon entry with hard_constraint=true (looked up via ref-query.sh against the canon corpus)
3. If yes, diffs the item's values{} block between first-pass and second-pass
4. If the diff is non-empty on a hard-constraint item, FAILS the coordination-pass and surfaces a clear error naming the mutated item + canon rule_id
5. After successful diff-check, re-runs the deterministic post-processor (from story 67c1) to refresh the checks block on mutated (non-hard-constraint) items

The diff-check is enforced before the second-pass artifact is accepted as the final output.

## Test Approach (Given/When/Then)
Given a first-pass artifact with one item citing a hard_constraint=true canon rule (e.g., uswds-forms.error-message-required-field) and one item citing a hard_constraint=false rule; When a synthetic coordination-pass second-pass artifact mutates BOTH items; Then the diff-check identifies the hard-constraint item's mutation, exits non-zero, and stderr names the offending item's stable_id + canon rule_id. Conversely, when the second-pass only mutates the non-hard-constraint item, the diff-check passes and the post-processor recomputes that item's checks block.
